title: Go: State Machine
description: Implement a flexible finite state machine in Go with typed states, events, guard conditions, and entry/exit actions.

steps.title: Define state and event types
steps.description: Define string types `State` and `Event` with constants for a document workflow (draft, review, published states; submit, approve, reject events). Create a `Transition` struct with From, To states and Event. Print the defined transitions to verify them.
hints: Use `type State string` and `type Event string` for type safety
The Transition struct should have fields: `From State`, `Event Event`, `To State`

verification.successMessage: State, Event types and Transition struct define the FSM vocabulary!
verification.failureMessage: Print your transition definitions showing From, Event, and To values.

steps.title: FSM struct with transition table
steps.description: Create an `FSM` struct with a `current State` and a `transitions map[State]map[Event]State`. Implement `AddTransition(from, event, to)` and `Send(event)` methods. `Send` looks up the transition and updates the current state. Print the state before and after each event.
hints: Use a nested map: `map[State]map[Event]State` for O(1) transition lookup
`Send(event)` should return an error if no transition exists for the current state+event
Print state changes with `fmt.Printf("State: %s -> %s\n", before, after)`

verification.successMessage: FSM correctly transitions between states based on events!
verification.failureMessage: Print the state before and after each transition using fmt.Printf.

steps.title: Guard functions on transitions
steps.description: Add guard support to the FSM. Define a `type Guard func() bool` and extend the transition table to include optional guards. Modify `Send(event)` to evaluate the guard before allowing the transition. Print "Transition blocked by guard" when a guard returns false.
hints: Create a `TransitionRule` struct with To, Guard fields instead of a plain State
A nil guard means the transition is always allowed
After updating the transition table, call `guard()` in `Send` and skip the transition if false

verification.successMessage: Guard functions prevent transitions when conditions are not met!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Transition blocked by guard' when a guard prevents a transition.

steps.title: Entry and exit action callbacks
steps.description: Extend the FSM with entry and exit callbacks. Define `type Action func()` and add `onEntry map[State][]Action` and `onExit map[State][]Action`. Call exit actions when leaving a state and entry actions when entering. Print "Entering <state>" and "Exiting <state>" messages.
hints: Register actions with `fsm.OnEntry(state, func() { ... })` and `fsm.OnExit(state, func() { ... })`
In `Send`, call exit actions of the current state before the transition, entry actions of the new state after
Actions are slices so multiple callbacks can be registered per state

verification.successMessage: Entry and exit callbacks fire correctly during state transitions!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Entering <state>' on entry and 'Exiting <state>' on exit.

steps.title: Nested states with parent hierarchy
steps.description: Implement nested states where a parent state contains substates. Define a `type CompoundState struct` with `Name` and `Initial` substate. Extend the FSM to handle substate transitions and inherit parent transitions. Print the full state path (e.g. "review.editing") after transitions.
hints: Store states as a hierarchical path string like "review.editing" for nested representation
When an event matches a parent transition, reset to the parent's initial substate

verification.successMessage: Nested states correctly inherit parent transitions and track substate paths!
verification.failureMessage: Print the full state path (e.g. 'review.editing') after each transition.
